items.title: The Remnant ledger's socket handed the whole answer key to any sender who asked (rm.ledgerRequest) and took rm.secret / rm.full from players
items.old_state: fixed in 1.2.43 (AUDIT-1.2.42.md 2.1; commit 90c17021): the handler takes senderId, refuses a non-GM and answers senderId only
items.evidence: The ledger has no socket of its own since E04 (remnants.mjs:1846-1852; commit 76cec7b6, 1.2.63): its rows travel as a GM store. gm-store.mjs:658-663 (gmsRefusal) refuses every gms.* packet when this client is no GM or when the user Foundry names as the sender is no GM (gm-store.mjs:1181-1195), before any answer; answers go to senderId alone (gm-store.mjs:1200-1201, 1218-1219). A grep of scripts/ for rm.ledger, rm.secret and rm.full finds nothing.
items.pinned_by: R170 (tier 1, 'GM replicas converge by the protocol, and nothing from a player or another world is taken'; tests-tier1.mjs:6603); scenario 61-gmstore-case check B5 (a player's gms.delta changes nothing on the GM; 61-gmstore-case.mjs:394-401)
items.refutation_tried: Looked for a second road that sends ledger rows to a non-GM: hello, state, delta and done all pass gmsRefusal first, the engine's listener is put up on GM clients only (gm-store.mjs:1741-1742), and the lists a player is sent are built on the GM (cleanup.mjs:215 cleanableTracesForPlayer).
items.note: Closed first in 1.2.43 by a senderId check; the handler itself went in E04. R170's player case is a delta; a player's gms.hello meets the same first lines of gmsRefusal (read; no test of its own found).

items.evidence: advanceIfDue is still the primary's alone (trial-floor.mjs:1721-1724), asked by a one-second tick on every client with an open floor (1821-1831) and on a tab's return (1778-1780). By the code another connected GM becomes the primary (utils.mjs:485-496) and its next tick writes the transition; with no GM connected nothing advances until a GM's ready starts the tick again (1766).

items.title: Live check 5: Move the body teleports the victim's token and the body's own move runs the discovery check; a room with two innocents fires the discovery at once - decide whether that is intended
items.old_state: not carried into section 7 or 9.2; no decision on it found
items.evidence: The trigger stands: every token move on the primary runs maybeBodyFound (murder-rules.mjs:3175-3190), the body's teleport included (cleanup.mjs:1987), and the check reads the moved token's room (body.mjs:781) and counts a death the GMs still keep as a body (body.mjs:654-668). The result changed: since 1.2.113 a count of two tells each witness privately, writes the room's discovery as waiting and asks the primary GM before anything is announced (body.mjs:813-850, the owner's decisions A and B of 13.11.2026 named there).
items.pinned_by: none found for a body carried into an occupied room
items.still_wrong: A killer's Move the body lands the body in a room where two students stand, one of them uninvolved: both are told privately at once and the GM is asked to announce, while the killer's Stage 6 still runs. Whether the body's own move should count as walking in is recorded nowhere.
items.refutation_tried: Checked whether the discovery is held while Stage 6 runs (it is not: the running incident's killers only count as involved, body.mjs:794-802) and where a kept death's body is read (its token, since it has no tile: body-tile.mjs:144-158).

not_established: Whether a veiled card whose words never reached a browser is hidden in a real v14 chat log. secret.mjs:1026-1032 sets display none on it; docs/dev/e58/LOCAL-REPORT.md:481 (LIVE-E06-01, 'measured, with a question') says the victim's chat showed three veiled cards with the placeholder after a failed opening. If they are drawn, a direct murder's victim sees that private cards were posted at that moment. Settled by: on a bystander's page during an opening, the computed display of the log's elements for those message ids.

CASE-08's remaining part: whether game.user can be null on Foundry v14 when a module socket listener registered at ready fires (a page closing). Settled by: v14's Game#user getter and its teardown, or the console of a tab closed while an opening invitation is sent to it.

CASE-LC2: whether the cast packet and the opening's invitation can arrive reversed, or the invitation before the listeners, on a real server. Settled by: a re-ask from the tracker in the seconds after the roller's reload, reading whether a roll window opens.

No test or scenario was found that would fail if these came back: the deleteToken tombstone (CASE-12), the refusal of words for another user's card (CASE-13 a), a bystander's trace elsewhere staying undecided (CASE-11, D5), the GM whisper after a noticed trap (CASE-10 c), the names of those still to vote (CASE-14). 'Not found' means a grep of test names and of the symbols in tests-tier0/1/2 and the scenarios, not a reading of their 194 222 lines.
The harness was not run by this reader: every 'pinned_by' is a test or check named in the source, and its result is the base run's to give.
